title: Body plethysmography
what: You sit in a clear booth and breathe into a tube. The device precisely measures your lung volume and how air moves through your airways.
why: When regular spirometry is not enough: to clarify lung disease, before lung surgery, or to track treatment.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; the report is usually ready the same day
tell_doctor: What inhalers and breathing medicines you use
If you recently had eye, chest, or belly surgery
If you recently had a heart attack or have heart disease
If you have a cold or a flare-up right now
If you are afraid of closed spaces. The booth is clear, and the door opens right away

prepare.title: Smoking and coffee
prepare.text: Do not smoke for at least a few hours. No coffee or strong tea in the morning.

prepare.title: Inhalers
prepare.text: Ask your doctor whether to use your inhalers before the test. Do not stop them on your own.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast 2 hours before. Do not eat a big meal.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes, with no tight belt.

steps: You sit in a clear booth, and the door is closed
A clip goes on your nose, and you hold the tube with your lips
The tube is closed for a second. Keep breathing gently
Sometimes you are asked to take a deep breath in and breathe out hard
After a few minutes, the door is opened
feel: The booth is closed but clear, and staff talk to you
When the tube is closed, breathing feels hard. It lasts 1 to 2 seconds
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready the same day

faq.q: What if I feel scared in the booth?
faq.a: Say so or wave your hand. The door will be opened right away.

faq.q: How is it different from spirometry?
faq.a: Spirometry measures your breath out. Body plethysmography shows the full lung volume, including what is left after breathing out.

reminders.text: Body plethysmography tomorrow. No smoking or coffee in the morning. Ask your doctor about your inhalers.
